Hi Irene,

Our renewal is coming due in late December (contract GLR-2024-RW). Usage has been higher than forecast — we expect an additional 60–80% embedding volume through Q1 and a seasonal surge in January. Before we lock anything in, Procurement asked whether Redwood can provide a short-term pricing lock or bridge that lets us commit to a larger capacity without taking on a full multi-year commit today.

High level asks:

- Option to convert a portion of the hold into a 12-month committed tranche if volume materializes

Hi Anna — thanks for the context and the forecast. Appreciate the clear asks. We can absolutely design a renewal that separates the immediate commercialization risk from the longer-term commit — a few approaches that tend to work for customers in your situation:

1) 90-day pricing lock + conditional convert: we hold your current committed price for 90 days. Within that window you can convert X% of forecasted uplift into a 12-month committed tranche. Conversion is one-sided (customer can convert; we do not force).

2) Bridge credits + burst pool: provide a finite burst pool (pre-funded credits) that applies to overage during the first 30–60 days post-renewal at a reduced overage rate. Unused credits can either be refunded or rolled into committed units at a discounted conversion rate.

3) Short-term uplift tranche: an interim committed tier (60–120 days) with a modest uplift over current rate, after which you can either drop back to prior commit or convert to long-term at a pre-agreed rate.

If you like, option 1 + 2 is often simplest operationally and gives procurement the price certainty they want while giving you runway to validate actual volume. I put a short summary together and attached it (initial-proposal-summary.pdf).

Would you be available for a call Thursday to walk through a draft term sheet? I’ll include Vanessa and Karthik to lock the pricing math and conversion mechanics.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposed term sheet — price hold + convert-to-commit + burst credits

Hi Anna — thanks for your patience while we ran the internal model and legal language. Attached is a concise term sheet that captures the approach we discussed: GreenLeaf-term-sheet-2027-11-10.pdf. Key points below so you have the highlights in email form:

1) 90-day Price Lock: Redwood will hold GreenLeaf's current committed unit price for 90 days from the execution date. The price lock is conditional on signing the attached SOW and a one-time booking fee equal to 10% of the agreed burst-credit value.

2) Convert-to-Commit Window: During the 90-day lock, GreenLeaf may convert up to 60% of the forecasted uplift into a 12-month committed tranche. Minimum conversion floor: 30% of uplift. Conversion triggers the pre-agreed committed rate in the term sheet.

3) Burst Credits: A 200k-token-equivalent burst pool will be made available for the first 60 days post-renewal at a reduced overage rate (60% of base overage). 50% of unused credits may be optionally rolled into committed units at a 10% conversion bonus if GreenLeaf elects conversion within the lock window. Credits are non-refundable except as rolled into committed units.

4) Operational notes: credits will be tracked at token-equivalent granularity and applied at time of billing. We will provide an interim usage dashboard for the 90-day period. DocuSign link is included in the term sheet for rapid signature.

Would you like us to set up a 30-minute review tomorrow to walk the numbers live? If this looks directionally right, we can issue the SOW for signature and activate the lock immediately on signature.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this along.

Best regards,
